coach.title: Personal AI Coach

welcome.0: Let's sharpen your Connect Four tactics.

coach.emptyQueue: No positions in queue — keep training to build your personal curriculum.

prompt.0: You can win right now — find the column.
prompt.1: There's an immediate winning move on the board. Can you spot it?
prompt.2: One move ends the game in your favor. Where do you play?

hint.0: Look for a row where you're one move from four in a row.
hint.1: Check each of your existing groups of three — is any of them one away from connecting?

optimal.0: Nice — you spotted the winning move.

suboptimal.0: Close — there was a faster win available.

prompt.0: Your opponent is about to win — stop them.
prompt.1: There's a forced block you must make. Find it.
prompt.2: One column is the only safe move. Which is it?

hint.0: Look for a row where your opponent is one move from four in a row.
hint.1: Check each of your opponent's groups of three — is any of them one away from connecting?

optimal.0: Well defended — you blocked the threat.

suboptimal.0: You blocked, but there was a cleaner defensive move.

blunder.0: That leaves your opponent's winning threat wide open.

prompt.0: Find the move that creates two winning threats at once.
prompt.1: One column sets up two simultaneous threats your opponent can't both stop.
prompt.2: Look for a fork — a move that threatens in two directions.

hint.0: Think about moves that add to two different groups at once.
hint.1: A double threat wins because your opponent can only block one.

optimal.0: Perfect — you created the double threat.

suboptimal.0: Good move, but a different column creates two threats at once.

blunder.0: That misses the chance to create two simultaneous threats.

prompt.0: As Yellow, you can secure a draw — find the Claimeven move.
prompt.1: Yellow has a drawing strategy here. Which column keeps it alive?
prompt.2: Use Claimeven: Yellow plays below every Red even-row threat.

hint.0: Look for an even row where Red has a threat — Yellow should mirror below it.
hint.1: Claimeven works by ensuring Yellow always gets the square directly below Red's even-row threats.

optimal.0: Exactly — that's the Claimeven move that secures the draw.

suboptimal.0: You're still in the draw zone, but the Claimeven key column was stronger.

blunder.0: That column gives up Yellow's Claimeven drawing advantage.

prompt.0: A Z-threat gives you unstoppable parity control — find it.
prompt.1: Use the Z-threat pattern to guarantee you get the winning odd-row square.
prompt.2: One column sets up Z-threat parity so your opponent can't stop you.

hint.0: Look for a column where your odd-row threat can't be claimed by your opponent.
hint.1: Z-threats work by creating a parity chain your opponent is forced to follow.

optimal.0: Spot on — you activated the Z-threat.

suboptimal.0: Reasonable move, but the Z-threat column creates stronger parity control.

blunder.0: That move hands away your Z-threat parity advantage.
